## Equilibrium conditions for several condensables (saturation adjustment) {#sec-ch04-conditions}

### Summary

Each condensation reaction turns gases into one condensate, for example water vapour into liquid water or ammonia
and hydrogen sulfide into solid ammonium hydrosulfide. At equilibrium, a reaction whose condensate is present has its
gas partial pressures on the saturation curve. A reaction whose condensate is absent may sit below that curve, but
never above it. kintera writes this per reaction with a product of partial pressures, so one rule covers a single
vapour and a reaction of two vapours alike. The condition is the one used for moist adiabats with several condensing
species.[^ch04-conditions-lio18]

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** The conditions every saturation-adjustment solve must satisfy (@eq-ch04-conditions-saturation).

**Data.** Gas mole fractions, condensate amounts, $T$ [K], $p$ [Pa]; one constant per reaction.

**Placement.** Inside both solvers of this chapter.

**Activation.** Always, for every reaction the thermodynamics options list.

**Guarantee / limits.** Satisfied to a tolerance in the logarithm, `ftol`.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer below.
:::

Local symbols: reaction $j$ with stoichiometric coefficient $\nu_{ij}$ of species $i$, positive for a gas consumed
by condensation; $x_i$ the mole fraction of species $i$ among all species; $x_{\mathrm{g}}$ the sum of the gas mole
fractions; $p_i = p\,x_i/x_{\mathrm{g}}$ the partial pressure [Pa] of gas $i$; $K_j(T)$ the saturation constant of
reaction $j$ [$\mathrm{Pa}^{\sum_i \nu_{ij}}$]; $c_j$ the amount of the condensate of reaction $j$; $\Delta_j$ its
saturation deficit (dimensionless), defined below.

### Derivation

The saturation constant of a reaction is the product of the partial pressures of its gases on the saturation curve,
each raised to its coefficient. For water vapour condensing it is the saturation vapour pressure; for ammonium
hydrosulfide it is the product of the ammonia and hydrogen sulfide partial pressures. Define the saturation deficit
of reaction $j$ as $\Delta_j = \ln K_j(T) - \sum_i \nu_{ij} \ln p_i$, positive when the gases are subsaturated. The
equilibrium conditions are then three complementarity relations, for every reaction $j$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
c_j &\ge 0, \\
\Delta_j &\ge 0, \\
c_j\,\Delta_j &= 0 .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch04-conditions-saturation}

In words: the condensate amount is never negative, the gases are never supersaturated, and a reaction whose
condensate is present sits exactly on its saturation curve.

The code tests these conditions in logarithms and in mole fractions. Taking the logarithm of the product and
substituting $p_i = p\,x_i/x_{\mathrm{g}}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\sum_i \nu_{ij} \ln p_i &= \sum_i \nu_{ij} \ln\frac{x_i}{x_{\mathrm{g}}} + \Big(\sum_i \nu_{ij}\Big) \ln p \\
\sum_i \nu_{ij} \ln\frac{x_i}{x_{\mathrm{g}}} &= \ln K_j(T) - \Big(\sum_i \nu_{ij}\Big) \ln p .
\end{aligned}
$$

The left side of the second line is what `equilibrate_tp` accumulates as `log_frac_sum`, and the right side is its
`logsvp[j]` ({{< code src/thermo/equilibrate_tp.h equilibrate_tp >}}). Equality is accepted when the two differ by
at most the tolerance `logsvp_eps`, which the callers set from the option `ftol`.

### Numerical method

No iteration here: this scheme defines the target. A reaction counts as out of equilibrium, and joins the active set
of the solvers, when either

1. its left side exceeds $\ln K_j + \epsilon$, so the gases are supersaturated and vapour must condense; or
2. its left side is below $\ln K_j - \epsilon$ while its condensate is present, so condensate must evaporate.

Here $\ln K_j$ stands for the right side of the second line above and $\epsilon$ for the tolerance `logsvp_eps`.

A reaction whose condensate is absent and whose gases are subsaturated stays out of the active set: the inequality
in @eq-ch04-conditions-saturation holds. Both tests are in `equilibrate_tp`
({{< code src/thermo/equilibrate_tp.h equilibrate_tp >}}).

### Limits

- Condensates are treated as pure phases with unit activity: their amount enters only through $c_j > 0$, never
  through the product. Solutions of condensates are not modelled.
- TODO: the behaviour when a gas of a reaction is absent from the cell; not measured.
